claim: V05 §3.16 (4)'s landfall table has no rule for a covered part already further down its ladder than the row's outcome. The wall row keeps a run already breached or dismantled ('the ladder only stepping down'). The raised row (l. 1342) writes `ruined` and the retaining row (l. 1343) writes `decayed`, with no such rule. V06 §3.19.2 (4) says 'a landfall ruins the spans and supports it covers whatever their state'. So a `cleared` span or support (its stone salvaged, V06 §3.19.2 (3)) is written back to `ruined`, and a `ruined` retaining run (its stone gone) back to `decayed`. The results are wrong: a released way counts as standing again (V06 §3.19.1 (3): 'every span standing or ruined, none cleared') and is repaired by V06 §3.19.2 (5), though 'a dismantled span or a cleared support is never rebuilt'; its 'rubble' is salvaged again, so the ledger credits the same stone twice; the retaining run is repaired by `repairRetaining` though 'a ruined stretch ... is not restored'; and a `cleared` member has no op to end its cover, so the decoration never closes. T-V5-14's new round-6 passage (l. 2562–2565) runs a landfall over a span 'already ... `cleared`' and 'a support by the run's band `cleared`' and asserts only 'by theirs'. A literal build passes the wrong result, while a builder reading the wall row's ladder keeps `cleared`.
required_change: V05 §3.16 (4), raised row: '`ruined` (item 244's span and support `state`);' -> '`ruined` (item 244's span and support `state`) — one already `ruined` kept, one already `cleared` (its stone taken, V06 §3.19.2 (3)) kept `cleared` and never a member, the state only stepping down as the wall row's ladder does;'. Retaining row: '`decayed` over its covered length (item 245's state,' -> '`decayed` over its covered length, a run of it already `ruined` (its stone gone) kept `ruined`, the state only stepping down (item 245's state,'. §3.16 (5): 'and the covered raised spans and raised-way piers, each by its raised way' -> 'and the covered raised spans and raised-way piers not `cleared`, each by its raised way'. §3.23's 'the landfall' row (l. 1774) adds the input 'a covered span or support already `cleared`; a covered retaining run already `ruined`' with the outcome 'kept as it is, no member' (T-V5-14). T-V5-14: 'a span over the run already `ruined` and, on a second run, `cleared`' -> '... `cleared` (kept `cleared`, no member, its way still released, V06 §3.19.1 (3))'; 'a support by the run's band `cleared`' -> '... `cleared` (kept `cleared`, no member)'. END V06 §3.19.2 (4): 'a landfall ruins the spans and supports it covers whatever their state' -> 'a landfall ruins the spans and supports it covers, standing or already `ruined`, a `cleared` one kept `cleared` (V05 §3.16 (4))'.
